subject: Why is this model identifiable? Number of free parameters VS. number of elements in var.-cov. matrix

messages.author: 20c442fe1ce5ac45
messages.subject: Why is this model identifiable? Number of free parameters VS. number of elements in var.-cov. matrix
parts:
Dear SEM Experts,

I am using both lavaan and Mplus. Could you help me, please? It is a very simple question, but I cannot find answer to it. I want to show in the first part of my work an extremely easy example of structural equation model (z1-z2 are latent variables, a1-a6 are measurement variables):

   MODEL:
              z1 BY a1 a2 a3;
              z2 BY a4 a5 a6;
              z2 ON z1;

Each manifest variable has 3 thresholds (4-1=3). Number of non-redundant parameters in the variance-covariance matrix is 6*(6+1)/2=21.

I am using WLSMV which is analogous to DWLS. Number of free parameters is 25, as there are 3*6=18 thresholds. Why is this model still identifiable? The t rule says that number of free parameters should be LESS or EQUAL to number of non-rendunat elements in the variance-covariance matrix.

Could you help me, please?

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Why is this model identifiable? Number of free parameters VS. number of elements in var.-cov. matrix
parts: Thresholds are not identified out of the variance - covariance matrix of the observed variables, but out of the crosstabs of the observed variables. The rule that you are using--identification depd=ends only on the unique elements of the covariance matrix--only applies to a subset of all structural equation models.
